subject: Proposed edits — support commitments & maintenance cadence (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Lisa Harper <procurement@stratacore.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@stratacore.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed edits — support commitments & maintenance cadence (MSA + Order Form)

Sean — thanks for the MSA + Order Form draft. Our procurement and ops teams reviewed and proposed a focused set of edits to the SLA/support sections. Attaching a tracked-changes doc (StrataCore_redlines_v2.docx) with inline commentary. High-level asks below so we can prioritize during legal review: 

- Uptime target: we moved the core API target to 99.95% to align with our internal SLAs; please confirm whether Redwood can accept 99.95% for the shared endpoint or if you will propose a separate premium tier.
- Service credits: proposal still ties credits to monthly uptime but we recommended a stepped credit schedule starting at 1% credit for 99.9–99.94% and scaling to 10% below 99.0%. We flagged language to ensure credits are not limited by a cap that prevents full remedy.
- Response times: request formal P1/P2/P3 response windows (P1: 1 hour, P2: 4 hours, P3: 24 hours) and a defined escalation ladder.
- Maintenance windows: propose no more than 8 hours/month of scheduled maintenance with 72-hour advance notice and an explicit blackout window during our weekly business hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 ET).
- Measurement: ask for telemetry access or aggregated uptime reports and the right to request raw incident logs for audit within 30 days.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on those bullets and loop in legal/product so we can converge quickly? We are aiming to complete legal review and have countersigned docs by 11/20 to meet our December launch.

Attachments: StrataCore_redlines_v2.docx (docx, tracked changes)

Thanks —
Lisa Harper
Senior Procurement Manager
StrataCore
procurement@stratacore.com

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Lisa Harper <procurement@stratacore.com>, Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@stratacore.com>

Date: 2026-11-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed edits — support commitments & maintenance cadence (MSA + Order Form)

Lisa — thanks for the detailed redlines and the tracked doc. We reviewed with product and support; copying legal and solutions to align on language. Quick summary of Redwood’s initial positions and proposed compromise: 

- Uptime: Our standard hosted offering targets 99.95% for production endpoints during the measurement period. We can accept 99.95% for the core API on the Order Form as requested if StrataCore agrees to the accompanying maintenance carveouts and telemetry measurement we propose (see attachments). If StrataCore needs a tighter guaranteed SLA for a single-tenant/dedicated pool, we can discuss Dedicated capacity pricing.

- Service credits: we are open to a stepped schedule but want to preserve a maximum aggregate credit per 12-month period to balance financial exposure. Kimberley/legal — please review proposed language in support_sla_matrix.xlsx (attached) and advise on acceptable cap language.

- Response times: Support tiering is achievable. We currently operate a P1 1-hour acknowledgement goal for incidents impacting production (with follow-through timelines driven by incident severity). We can formalize P1: 1 hour ack, P2: 4 hours, P3: 24 hours as contractual response definitions.

- Maintenance: We cannot agree to a hard 8 hours/month blackout without knowing the operational profile; our recommendation is: maximum 12 hours/month scheduled maintenance with calendarized windows, 72-hour notice for standard maintenance and 7-day notice for major upgrades, and an explicit ability to exercise emergency maintenance for security/critical fixes (with post-hoc notification).

Next step: Kimberley/legal, can you provide a marked-up counter to StrataCore’s doc focusing on the credit cap, measurement method (UTC day / rolling 30-day), and force majeure carveouts? Also, Jonas/product — happy to set a 30-minute working session with StrataCore ops tomorrow or Friday to walk through measurement telemetry and any dedicated-region options.

Attachments: support_sla_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

—Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Lisa Harper <procurement@stratacore.com>, Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@stratacore.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Proposed edits — support commitments & maintenance cadence (MSA + Order Form)

Lisa / Tom / Sean — looping in formal legal positions so the redline conversation has explicit drafting proposals. I’ve reviewed StrataCore_redlines_v2.docx and the support_sla_matrix.xlsx Sean shared. My high-level comments and proposed language edits below (I will deliver a tracked PDF by EOD):

- Measurement & audit: propose a clause that uptime is measured over a 30-day rolling window using server-side telemetry aggregated at the tenant level. Redwood will provide a monthly uptime report; StrataCore may request a one-time audit package (aggregated logs and incident timelines) once per 12-month period subject to NDAs and redaction for third-party data.

- Credits & cap: our preferred formulation is a stepped credit schedule (we accept the steps you proposed) with an annual aggregate cap equal to three (3) months' average monthly fees. This cap is negotiable for dedicated commitments; please advise your procurement if the cap is a hard blocker.

- Maintenance windows and blackout periods: counterproposal language — Scheduled Maintenance: "Customer agrees to a maximum of twelve (12) hours of scheduled maintenance per calendar month, provided Provider gives at least seventy-two (72) hours' notice. Provider will not schedule planned maintenance that materially degrades Customer production during the Customer blackout window as listed in the Order Form, absent emergency security fixes." We will not accept a blanket blackout for standard incident response.

- Escalations & remedies: include a three-tier escalation path (SE -> CS Director -> VP Support) with contact SLAs and a 30-day remediation plan for recalcitrant P1 regressions. Also propose terminating remedies tied to prolonged systemic failure (but with cure period).

- Force majeure & exclusions: clarity that third-party cloud outages and customer's misconfiguration are carveouts; propose language for the mutual cooperation during incidents and a defined dispute resolution timeline (30 days to engage technical arbitration).

I’ll produce a marked-up Order Form and MSA excerpts for StrataCore to review. In the meantime, can the StrataCore ops team confirm the blackout window time zone reference (your prior note used ET; please confirm DST handling)? Also, Sean — please hold open Friday 11/12 10:00–10:30 PT for a technical/ops call if that works for StrataCore.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
